summary: Ngulchu Dharmabhadra (1772–1851) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashi Gephel Monastery under Lobzang Tsultrim, Ngulchu Ngawang Dorje, and Lobpön Lozang Gyaltsen, and taught several prominent disciples.
Nguyen Thi Tuyet is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Punjabi University, attested in 2012, supervised by Inder Mohan Singh and traditional teacher Thich Nu Bao Nguyet.
Nguyen Thi Xinh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann, attested in 2013.
Nguyen Van Hoa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University under the doctoral supervision of Shailaja Bapat and Lata Chhatre.
Nguyen Van Thuong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi, where he completed an MA supervised by Karam Tej Singh Sarao.

Nguyễn Ngọc Ánh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at VNU-HCM (BA 2011–2015), University of Delhi (MA 2016–2018), and University of Economics and Law (LLB 2021–2023), and was a PhD scholar at University of Colombo in 2020.
Nhu Lien is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University under the teacher Ādiccavaṃsa.
Nhung Lu Rots works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied as a stipendiat at the University of Oslo (attested 2026), where she holds a post as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026.

Nianzu Huang (1913–1992) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Beijing Institute of Technology (~1932–1936) and under teachers including Lianju Xia, Nordan Hutuktu, and Gongga Rinpoche. He headed the Central People's Broadcasting Station and became a professor at BUPT (~1953).

Nichidatsu Fujii (1885–1985) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who founded Nipponzan-Myohoji. He studied at Rissho University (1912), Taisho University, Koyasan University, Horyuji Kangakuin, and Kennin-ji, and taught Gyoryo Maruyama.

Nicholas Dirks (1950–) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Wesleyan (~1968–1972) and Chicago (~1972–1981), he held faculty posts at Caltech (~1978–1987), Michigan (~1987–1997), and Columbia (~1997–2013).

Nicholas Justin Allen (1939–2020) specialized in Indology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Oxford under Rodney Needham, he taught at Durham (1972–1976) and served as Reader in the Social Anthropology of South Asia at Oxford and Wolfson College.

Nicholas Poppe (1897–1991) was a linguist and scholar of Central Asia and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, where he later became a professor (1925–1941), and concluded his career as Professor of Mongolian at the University of Washington (1949–1968).

Nicholas Roerich (1874–1947) worked in history, archaeology, Central Asian studies, and religious studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University and the Imperial Academy of Arts, he directed the Imperial Society for the Encouragement of the Arts and founded Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.

Nicholas Thanissaro specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Manchester (BSc 1982–1985), Manchester Metropolitan University (PGCE 1985–1986), University of Warwick (PhD 2010–2016), and the University of South Wales (MA 2017).

Nicholas Witkowski specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing his PhD at Stanford (2015) and a postdoc at the University of Tokyo (2015–2017), he held assistant professorships at Nanyang Technological University (2018) and the University of San Diego (2022).
Nicholson T. Collier is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Paul J. Griffiths.

Nicol Macnicol (1870–1952) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned an MA (~1887–1891) and D.Litt. (-1901) from the University of Glasgow. He served as a missionary at Wilson College, Mumbai, in 1895.

Nicola Bajetta is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Bajetta studied as a doctoral local researcher and worked as a research project staff member (Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter) at the University of Hamburg.

Nicola Di Cosmo (1957–) is a historian of Central Asia and Sinology. After receiving his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (~1987–1991), he taught at Harvard, Canterbury, and Columbia before joining the Institute for Advanced Study as a professor in ~2003.
